html:
The Bulgarian Empire was the medieval state of the Bulgarians in the eastern Balkans, between the Danube and the Aegean. It lasted, with a break, from 681 to 1396. The map labels it "Bulgar Khanate" from 1000 to 1400, including the 1100s when it was in fact under Byzantine rule.

The Bulgars under Asparuh settled south of the Danube in 681 and ruled the Slavs there. Khan Boris I accepted Christianity in 864, the conversion of Bulgaria. Under his son Simeon I the state took the title of tsar and became a centre of Slavic writing, where the Cyrillic script took shape.

The Byzantine emperor Basil II wore the empire down; after his victory at Kleidion in 1014 he conquered it by 1018. The uprising of Asen and Peter in 1185 founded the Second Bulgarian Empire, with its capital at Tarnovo. It fell to the Ottomans between 1393 and 1396. Modern Bulgaria came back in 1878.
